newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond spreads mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond spreads mostly unchanged.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond spreads were unchanged in quiet trade as long U.S. Treasuries gained more ground on Monday, dealers said.

In the high-yield market, price gains of 1/4 point were common with select names outperforming the pack. New issue activity dominated the session, traders noted, and strong aftermarket activity underpinned the tone.
Among issues priced were $200 million seven-year 144A overfunded senior notes from Renaissance Cosmetics Inc, priced at par to yield 11-3/4 percent via a CIBC Wood Gundy group.

Also, Advanced Radio Telecom Corp issued $135 million 10-year overfunded senior notes at par to yield 14 percent via lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co Inc. The issue was priced with warrants for 12 percent of the company, a source said.

In company specific news, Claridge Hotels and Casino's 11-3/4 percent notes rose into the mid-80s as investors gave credence to talk that the debt will be redeemed at par in a proposed acquisition by Hilton Hotels Corp, traders said. The debt rose about 10 points on Friday after Claridge said it was in acquisition talks with Hilton.

Back in high-grades, traders said spreads had a firmer bias even as long Treasuries posted better than 1/2 point gains following a softer-than-expected report on manufacturing. The report, from the National Association of Purchasing Management, also served to confirm expectations the Federal Reserve would leave interest rates unchanged at its policy-setting meetings this week.
The 30-year T-bond closed up 19/32 to yield 6.74 percent.
Capital Security issuance trickled in ahead of what most believe will be the negation of their dividend's tax-exempt status in the Clinton Administration budget proposal.
BT Preferred Capital Trust issued $250 million (10 million shares of $25 securities) 40-year trust preferreds with an 8-1/8 percent dividend.
Looking ahead, Philip Morris is expected to issue $500 million 10-year notes on Tuesday through Lehman Brothers.

Sherwin-Williams is expected to issue $700 million in a multi-tranche debt deal. The company's senior debt rating was cut to single-A from A-plus on Monday by Standard & Poor's rating agency citing higher-than-expected financial risk following the January debt-financed purchase of Thompson Minwax Holding Corp for $830 million.
